title: Make the reference system's views readable
description:
Decided by the owner on 2026-09-25 after looking at the merged views of madarch-mk5. Rendered by GitHub's own Mermaid renderer in a 1150 px column (a wide screen), 5 of the 8 pages show arrow labels under 12 px (the landscape 7.8 px, storefront 8.3 px, fulfilment 9.6 px, platform 11.7 px, ordering 11.9 px) and 7 of 8 have labels overlapping each other or a box. ## Done when
On every page of the reference system rendered by GitHub's Mermaid in a 1150 px column, arrow labels
are at least 12 px and no label overlaps another label or a box (measured by rendering every page
and recorded with the numbers); every arrow carries its row number and every relation behind it is
in that row of the table under its diagram; a topic's publishers and subscribers are marked
(action: send | receive), their arrows drawn from the initiator, dashed, and entered by role; in an
element's own view its module's refinement is drawn, not the general relation from its frame;
likec4 validate and the Mermaid parse still pass.
(Rewritten 2026-09-27 by the owner's decisions: arrows from the initiator instead of from the broker
(madarch-48x.1), and numbered arrows instead of word labels after measurement.)

## Left out
Direct producer-to-consumer arrows through a topic (a derived relation, a later decision); views per environment or state; the server.

title: Decide how the model marks a topic's or queue's consumer
description:
A decision the owner holds (asked 2026-09-25). Recommendation: (1).

Affects: the task that draws events from the broker to the consumer. Meanwhile the labels and the refinement tasks proceed.

title: Decide whether the server needs a restartable query-engine process
description:
A decision the owner holds, for the server of this outcome: whether the query engine must run in a separate process restarted after N queries or M megabytes.

## Corrected 2026-09-25
This decision was filed on a stage-3 reviewer's single measurement that read as a LadybugDB defect: memory growing by about 85 KB per recursive query with a time filter, flat without it. Checked since, that reading is wrong. The filter clause makes no difference; the growth comes from our own configuration, with LadybugDB's default of one execution thread per core and a new statement prepared for every query time, and from synchronous test loops that never let the runtime release dropped statements. The measurements and the fix are in madarch-ti6.2.

## Affects
The server of this outcome, which runs for days. Not views, the agent skill, or the foundation's correctness.

## Recommendation
No restartable process. Once madarch-ti6.2 lands, its long-run test shows whether memory levels off; if it does, the server holds one engine for its lifetime, rebuilt only when the history changes, and this decision closes on that evidence. If it still grows, the restartable process (rebuilt from the history, which is fast and exact) is the fallback.

## Meanwhile
Nothing waits on this before the server is built; madarch-ti6.2's result releases it.

title: Bound the query engine's memory by limiting LadybugDB's threads and not preparing a statement per query time
description:
Found 2026-09-25 while checking the recorded cause behind the server's memory decision (madarch-ti6.1). Measured with LadybugDB 0.20.4 under Bun 1.4.2 and Node 26, on a 14-core machine, 10 000 to 40 000 queries per run.

## What was measured
- The filter clause in a recursive query is not the cause: with and without it, memory grows the same and levels off (about 115 MB for 30 000 queries of a 200-node chain returning a count).
- Returning the path's relations (`rels(p)`, with or without `list_transform`) costs memory per execution thread. At the default thread count (one per core, 14 here) a process running `dependents` settles between 0.7 and 1.2 GB for a 50-element graph; with 1 or 2 threads (`new Connection(db, n)` or `setMaxNumThreadForExec`) it settles near 170 to 250 MB, and each query is about twice as fast (2.3 ms against 5.4 ms).
- `dependencyQuery` writes `valid`/`known` into the statement text (LadybugDB refuses `$parameters` inside a recursive relationship filter: "Cannot evaluate $_ because it does not depend on n or r", tried in five forms). A caller asking "now" through an advancing clock therefore prepares a new statement on every call: our engine at 2 threads, fixed time, stays at 253 MB over 40 000 calls; with an advancing time it climbs towards 1 GB.
- A prepared statement dropped by our code is released only when Node or Bun run its native finalizer, after garbage collection and an event-loop turn. A synchronous loop that never yields fills the 256 MB buffer pool within 10 000 distinct statements; with a yield every 500 calls 40 000 distinct statements plateau near 340 MB, under both runtimes. This is not a LadybugDB defect, and a server yields between requests.

## Done when
- the engine's connection runs with a small fixed number of threads (1 or 2, chosen by measurement);
- a query's `valid`/`known` are reduced to the latest time in the model history at or before them (the answer can change only at those times), so the statement texts are bounded by the history's size and the prepared-statement cache hits; the graph-queries conformance tests pass unchanged;
- a long-run test (at least 20 000 `dependents` and `view` calls with an advancing clock, yielding to the event loop between batches) shows memory levelling off under a stated bound, and is skipped with the other performance tests under `MADARCH_SKIP_PERF`;
- the code's statements that blamed LadybugDB are corrected: the engine's comments that a prepared statement is "never freed" and the B1 stability test's explanation of its growth (decision 0009 and `docs/system/index.md` were corrected when this was filed), and `docs/system/index.md`'s known unknown is updated to the measured result;
- an issue asking LadybugDB to accept parameters inside recursive relationship filters is drafted and shown to the owner; it is sent only with their yes.

## Left out
A worker process restarted after N queries (the open decision madarch-ti6.1 waits on this measurement); replacing the Node binding (the C API through Bun's FFI or the WASM build: both cost more and change nothing measured here).

title: Connect a fresh clone with one committed command and sign commits with the owner's public email
description:
Found while connecting a clone on the owner's second computer (2026-09-24).

## Owner decision
Commits are signed with the owner's public email (the one shown on the GitHub profile), not the GitHub noreply address: it is already public, so hiding it buys nothing. The integration's rule 'Commits use the GitHub noreply address' and the fresh-clone step 'set user.email to the noreply address' change accordingly. Past noreply commits stay as they are.

## Problems
- Connecting a fresh clone is six manual steps listed in .shady2k/integration.md (hooks path, the br-portable-path filter, private patterns, br import and source-path migration). Git never applies repository config on clone, so this cannot be automatic, but it can be one committed command.
- The private pattern list lives only in .git/info/private-patterns of each clone, so a second machine starts without it.
- .githooks/privacy-guard.sh exits 0 when that file is missing: an unconnected clone passes any staged content silently.

## Done when
- one committed command connects a fresh clone (hooks path, filter, br import and path migration, private patterns) and is idempotent on a connected one;
- the guard reads patterns from .git/info/private-patterns and from a documented per-user location outside the repository (synced by the owner), and refuses a commit, saying how to connect, when neither exists;
- the integration states the public-email rule and names the command as the fresh-clone step;
- proved on a fresh clone: before connecting, a commit is refused with the connect hint; after connecting, the hooks reject planted violations.

## Left out
No global git config is written by the command; syncing the pattern file between machines is the owner's own tooling.
close_reason: Done by the setup 0.26.0 update (madarch-kwe): sh .shady2k/connect.sh connects a fresh clone and is safe to rerun; the privacy guard reads a per-user and a per-clone list and refuses without one; the integration states the public-email rule and names the command; proved on fresh clones.
